EightPuzzle.__init__:
[DEFINE_WORKER: "Initializes the puzzle state by storing the provided initial board configuration and defining the standard solved goal state." __init__]
    [INPUTS]
        <REF> initial_state </REF>: list "The initial 8-puzzle board configuration as a nested list of integers; stored by reference into self.initial_state."
    [END_INPUTS]

    [OUTPUTS]
    [END_OUTPUTS]

    [MAIN_FLOW]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Store the provided initial_state reference into self.initial_state. RESULT self.initial_state]
            [COMMAND Create the constant nested list [[1, 2, 3], [4, 5, 6], [7, 8, 0]] as the goal state and assign it to self.goal_state. RESULT self.goal_state]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_MAIN_FLOW]

[END_WORKER]
EightPuzzle.find_blank:
[DEFINE_WORKER: "Scans a fixed 3x3 grid in row-major order and returns the coordinates of the first cell containing 0, or None if no such cell exists." find_blank]
    [INPUTS]
        <REF> state </REF>: 2D list/array of integers "A 3x3 grid represented as a list of lists, where 0 marks a blank cell."
    [END_INPUTS]

    [OUTPUTS]
        <REF> result </REF>: tuple(int, int) or None "The (row, column) coordinates of the first zero found, or None if the grid contains no zero."
    [END_OUTPUTS]

    [MAIN_FLOW]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Iterate over rows i from 0 to 2 inclusive using the outer for loop range(3). RESULT i]
            [COMMAND Within the outer loop over i, iterate over columns j from 0 to 2 inclusive using the inner for loop range(3). RESULT j]
            [COMMAND Within the nested loops, check whether state[i][j] equals 0. RESULT zero_found]
            [COMMAND If zero_found is true, return the tuple (i, j) immediately, exiting both loops and the function. RESULT return_value]
            [COMMAND If all 9 cells are checked and no zero is found, return None implicitly. RESULT return_value]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_MAIN_FLOW]

[END_WORKER]
EightPuzzle.move:
[DEFINE_WORKER: "Moves the blank tile one step in the requested direction by swapping it with an adjacent tile in a shallow copy of the puzzle state and returns the updated state." move]
    [INPUTS]
        <REF> state </REF>: list of lists "Current puzzle state represented as a matrix of rows; must contain a blank cell and support row slicing."
        <REF> direction </REF>: string "Direction to move the blank cell: 'up', 'down', 'left', or 'right'."
    [END_INPUTS]

    [OUTPUTS]
        <REF> new_state </REF>: list of lists "A shallow copy of state with the blank cell swapped with the adjacent tile in the requested direction; nested row objects are shared with state."
    [END_OUTPUTS]

    [MAIN_FLOW]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Locate the blank cell by calling self.find_blank(state) and unpack the returned pair into i as the row index and j as the column index. RESULT i, j]
            [COMMAND Create new_state as a shallow copy of state by iterating over each row and copying each row with row[:]. RESULT new_state]
            [COMMAND Within the if/elif chain on direction, if direction is 'up', swap new_state[i][j] with new_state[i - 1][j]. RESULT new_state]
            [COMMAND Within the same if/elif chain, if direction is 'down', swap new_state[i][j] with new_state[i + 1][j]. RESULT new_state]
            [COMMAND Within the same if/elif chain, if direction is 'left', swap new_state[i][j] with new_state[i][j - 1]. RESULT new_state]
            [COMMAND Within the same if/elif chain, if direction is 'right', swap new_state[i][j] with new_state[i][j + 1]. RESULT new_state]
            [COMMAND If direction is not one of 'up', 'down', 'left', or 'right', make no swap in new_state. RESULT new_state]
            [COMMAND Return new_state. RESULT new_state]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_MAIN_FLOW]

[END_WORKER]
EightPuzzle.get_possible_moves:
[DEFINE_WORKER: "Computes the valid slide directions for the blank space in the given puzzle state based on its row and column position." get_possible_moves]
    [INPUTS]
        <REF> state </REF>: object "Puzzle state object passed to find_blank to locate the blank position."
    [END_INPUTS]

    [OUTPUTS]
        <REF> moves </REF>: list "List of valid move strings, each one of 'up', 'down', 'left', 'right'."
    [END_OUTPUTS]

    [MAIN_FLOW]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Initialize moves as an empty list. RESULT moves]
            [COMMAND Call self.find_blank(state) and unpack its returned row and column into i and j respectively. RESULT i, j]
            [COMMAND If i > 0, append the string 'up' to moves. RESULT moves]
            [COMMAND If i < 2, append the string 'down' to moves. RESULT moves]
            [COMMAND If j > 0, append the string 'left' to moves. RESULT moves]
            [COMMAND If j < 2, append the string 'right' to moves. RESULT moves]
            [COMMAND Return moves. RESULT moves]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_MAIN_FLOW]

[END_WORKER]
EightPuzzle.solve:
[DEFINE_WORKER: "Performs a breadth-first search from self.initial_state to self.goal_state, returning the shortest path as a list of moves, or None if no such path exists." solve]
    [INPUTS]
    [END_INPUTS]

    [OUTPUTS]
        <REF> result </REF>: list of moves or None "The shortest path from self.initial_state to self.goal_state as a list of moves, or None if no path exists."
    [END_OUTPUTS]

    [MAIN_FLOW]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Initialize open_list as a list containing a single tuple (self.initial_state, []). RESULT open_list]
            [COMMAND Initialize closed_list as an empty list. RESULT closed_list]
            [COMMAND Start the BFS loop: continue while open_list is non-empty. RESULT open_list]
            [COMMAND Inside the while loop, pop the first (oldest) element from open_list and unpack it into current_state and path. RESULT current_state, path]
            [COMMAND Inside the while loop, append current_state to closed_list. RESULT closed_list]
            [COMMAND Inside the while loop, if current_state is not the goal, iterate over each move returned by self.get_possible_moves(current_state). RESULT move]
            [COMMAND Inside the for loop over moves, compute new_state by calling self.move(current_state, move). RESULT new_state]
            [COMMAND Inside the for loop over moves, if new_state is not contained in closed_list, append the tuple (new_state, path + [move]) to open_list. RESULT open_list]
            [COMMAND After the while loop exits because open_list is empty, return None. RESULT None]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_MAIN_FLOW]

    [ALTERNATIVE_FLOW: Inside the while loop, after appending current_state to closed_list, current_state equals self.goal_state]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Return path immediately as the successful BFS result. RESULT path]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_ALTERNATIVE_FLOW]

[END_WORKER]
